Welcome to /v/Perk the Voat verse devoted to Perk and perkers.
Perk is a website and set of mobile apps for making extra money online.

Perk rewards with both Points and Tokens, Points can be converted to GCs at a rate of 1000 pts to approximately $1.00 it can vary depending on the GC you choose. Tokens are more like website currency you use them to join sweepstakes.

The Apps

These are the main way that people earn cash on perk.

There is a lot of speculation about the app limits, only Perk knows for sure. Formerly the Perk TOS said that you were allowed to run each app on 5 devices per account with 1 account per person i.e. 5 phones running PerkTV, 5 phones running pop quiz, 5 phones running Live etc. No one really knows for sure, but it’s generally considered to still be true and a large number of Perkers have reported running 5 per app and not having problems in the months since Perk changed their TOS.
However, there are some sporadic reports of people having rewards cancelled for running Pop quiz on 5 phones at once and some for running Live and tapping to quickly, so YMMV, Perk is generally pretty good about restoring rewards if you contact them.

PerkTV is the main app it’s available on Android, IOS and Kindle, you choose a category and it will show you one video followed by one advertisement, right now that will earn you from 1-3 points, mostly 1 point.

Perk Pop Quiz on Android and IOS answer trivia questions and earn points. In normal mode you earn 1 point per round of 5 questions each question has a 10 second timer. In Lightning mode (accessible in settings) you earn 2 points per round with a 5 second timer. Both modes reward more points for correct answers.

PerkTV Live Android only Listens to your television and plays ads during commercials. Sounds weird, right? It is a bit, after you run the app i9t will have to be activated, the little red light in the upper right corner will have to turn green, by hearing TV audio, perk itself says you can use any source for this including netflix, then choose a TV show any TV show it doesn’t have to be the one you are watching, your device listens for commercial breaks and plays Perks own ads when it hears them. You get a maximum of 5 ads per commercial break paying 3 pts per ad. Sometimes you get fewer than 5 ads though. You can also activate the ads by tapping the throbbing red circles at the bottom of the app.

Perk Screen Android only use perk as your lock screen, plays ads when you unlock for points.

Search&Win Android and IOS self explanatory, search and randomly win points.

Prize Mob Android and IOS spend tokens to bid on prizes.

Perk Wallet Android and IOS keeps track of all your perk rewards and gives discounts on some reward GCs

Perk Shopping Android and IOS find coupons online and earn Perk points when shopping at supported stores.

Scratch&Win Android and IOS Win Points, tokens and prizes playing a scratch off game on your phone.

Perk Browser Android and IOS

The website

Not as many use the website for money making, but it can be a good way to earn extra points if you don’t mind being interactive.

Special offers are under the Quick points menu, they allow you to make points by taking surveys, sweepstakes offers, download apps and other click work.

Sweepstakes reward points by spending tokens or points. always be sure to check which currency the entry fee is in.

If you negotiate to pay in advance all cash money, you can often get a better price than insurance companies get. Its people who do not try to have relatives pay in a timely manner or appoint someone to negotiate for you if it is an emergency.

If they think you are not going to pay they hit you with the most so the later reduced negotiated settlement that is actually paid is close to the cost of care, or includes a modest profit.

No one pays what they are first billed - if you have been you are doing it wrong.

I am not defending the system just that the title does not reflect what is finally paid in settlement. Also many uninsured never pay a penny. Never ever.
Who would you negotiate with. It's not a mechanic.
For me it was the door at the back of the complex labeled "Billing". It was like dealing with a shitty used car salesman. It cost me a free 10 minute conversation with a lawyer to prep for it.

Yeah, no shit. I wonder if people who have always had insurance have ever seen a medical bill for someone who isn't insured, cause if not I could understand how they would think everyone who has delinquent medical expenses is lazy.

The bill says they charged you $15,212.54 for some IV aspirin and a plaster splint. The invoice says they "forgave" half of it and you "only" owe $7,5106.27. Then collections gets an amount of $6,000 even, and tells you the hospital is "willing to settle" for $4,997 if you pay it TODAY. It's fucking ridiculous. But it's Obama's fault that the insurance companies are charging off-exchange families "10x what I paid before!"

That's because when hospitals charge insurance companies, they have the resources to negotiate down whatever price is thrown at them. When someone is uninsured, they gouge them because even if that person tried to contest the cost, they would likely not have any leverage because it's not like if they knocked it down $5k he would pay, and debt purchasers would buy the debt no matter the cost (hell, the higher the cost the better, it takes longer to pay off and the debt collection agency would make a long, steady stream of interest), at which point it's their problem.
